# `kubectl` from MSYS / Git-Bash on Windows: Path Translation

MSYS / Git-Bash on Windows rewrites POSIX-style paths inside `kubectl.exe`
argv elements before kubectl sees them. The rewrite happens whether the path
is local or pod-side, and it breaks two common command shapes:

- `kubectl cp <local> <pod>:<remote>` — `~/...` and `/...` local paths get
  translated to `C:\...`. `kubectl cp` then parses the leading `C:` as the
  `[namespace/]pod:path` delimiter and treats both arguments as remote
  specs. Error: `error: one of src or dest must be a local file
  specification`.
- `kubectl exec <pod> -- <cmd> <args>` — absolute paths in the post-`--`
  argv (e.g. `/var/run/...`) get translated to `C:\Program Files\Git\var\run\...`
  before the wire call. The in-pod process then runs `mkdir -p 'C:/...'`,
  `ls -l 'C:/...'`, or `sh -c 'cat > C:/...'` and fails with
  `mkdir: can't create directory 'C:/': Permission denied` or similar.

The same recipes work unchanged on WSL and native Linux because no path
translation layer exists there.

## Rule 1: Replace `kubectl cp` with a stdin pipe

Local paths on the host side of a shell pipe are not in `kubectl`'s argv,
so MSYS leaves them alone:

```bash
cat <local-file> | kubectl exec -i <pod> -c <container> -- sh -c 'cat > <remote-path>'
```

The `<remote-path>` inside the single-quoted `sh -c` string is opaque to
MSYS (single quotes prevent argv splitting before the `sh -c` runs in the
pod), so absolute pod-side paths survive.

## Rule 2: Use relative paths for `kubectl exec -- <cmd> <args>` targets

When the container's working directory is `/` (true for most images), use
relative paths in the post-`--` argv:

```bash
# Wrong on MSYS — /var/run gets rewritten to C:\Program Files\Git\var\run
kubectl exec <pod> -c <container> -- mkdir -p /var/run/claude/.claude

# Right — relative path, in-pod shell resolves against cwd=/
kubectl exec <pod> -c <container> -- mkdir -p var/run/claude/.claude
```

Document the cwd assumption in the recipe so future readers can verify
against `kubectl exec -- pwd` if the container image changes.

## Alternative: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`

```bash
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 kubectl exec <pod> -- ls -l /var/run/claude/.claude
```

Disables path translation for one invocation. Heavier hammer than the
stdin-pipe + relative-path forms — every absolute path in the command must
already be in the correct form for both shells. Prefer Rule 1 and Rule 2;
reach for `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV` only when neither fits (e.g. a tool that
genuinely requires an absolute path argument).

## When to apply

- Any Makefile target, runbook step, or script that drives `kubectl.exe`
  and might be invoked from Git-Bash / MSYS / Cygwin on Windows.
- The relative-path form (Rule 2) still works on WSL and native Linux, so
  a target written for the worst case is portable.
